PiSsh iOS third-party notices

libssh2 1.11.1
Copyright the libssh2 project and its contributors.
BSD-3-Clause; complete license in libssh2/COPYING and individual source headers.
Source: https://libssh2.org/download/libssh2-1.11.1.tar.gz
Archive SHA256: d9ec76cbe34db98eec3539fe2c899d26b0c837cb3eb466a56b0f109cabf658f7
Release/tag: https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/tree/libssh2-1.11.1
This directory contains the release's include/*.h and src/*.{c,h}.

Local modifications (semantic changes marked PiSsh in the affected files):
- src/chacha.h removes one trailing blank line to pass git diff --check; no
  code or license text is changed.
- src/channel.c initializes a newly opened channel's exit_status to -1, rather
  than implicit zero, to preserve the JS contract for absent SSH exit-status.
- src/kex.c frees the old server_hostkey before replacing it during ECDH and
  curve25519 rekey. The DH path already does this in the upstream release.
- src/mac.c makes the integrated AES-GCM MAC return free_key=1: it does not
  retain the generated MAC key. Otherwise each exchange leaks that buffer.
- src/openssl.c frees key_fromdata_ctx, peer_key and bn_ctx in the OpenSSL 3
  ECDH shared-secret function's cleanup path. They are temporary owned objects.
The latter three changes fix leaks reproduced by the portable ASan/LSan tests.
- src/openssl.h includes through PiSshOpenSSL.h's namespace macro: the CocoaPod
  selects OpenSSL.framework directly; portable builds use ordinary OpenSSL
  headers. No crypto behavior changes. This avoids filesystem-case collisions
  and shadowing of the framework's modular headers.
Additional PiSsh nonblocking lifecycle delta (upstream archive hashes unchanged):
- include/libssh2.h and src/session.c expose two local worker-only extensions:
  session_pending_operation reports pending ciphertext or key exchange (not an
  ordinary inbound wait); session_abort is terminal no-I/O destruction after
  socket shutdown. Abort marks the socket disconnected before channel cleanup,
  discards pending ciphertext, and uses the normal resource destructors. It
  checks the destructor result rather than abandoning a session on EAGAIN.
- src/transport.c rejects sends on a disconnected session before entering KEX
  or comparing pending packet addresses; abort cannot resume any network I/O.
- src/channel.c keeps an outbound/KEX EAGAIN visible rather than masking it with
  buffered channel payload. The core can then resume exactly that API before
  another operation starts a competing packet or rekey.
- src/channel.c also keeps channel writes in their input-draining state when
  a global-request reply is partially sent. Retrying cannot skip that reply
  and replace it with channel data; a deterministic reply-backpressure test
  exercises both EAGAIN and partial socket writes.
- src/channel.c and src/libssh2_priv.h keep the five-byte EOF packet in the
  channel, not on the stack: transport's pointer-identity continuation contract
  requires stable storage across retries and EOF calls nested inside close.
- src/packet.c only treats positive transport results as packet types and keeps
  waiting when a reply belongs to another channel. A zero/no-packet result must
  not match the packet-type string terminator, and an unmatched reply must not
  become a fatal -1. Deterministic packet-wait regressions preserve both cases.
These changes are exercised by Linux --wrap=send EAGAIN/partial-send tests against
production core code, including repeated rekey and cancellation under blocked
sends. No protocol checks, host pin checks, or signature verification are removed.

OpenSSL 3.6.2
Copyright The OpenSSL Project Authors. All Rights Reserved.
Apache-2.0; full license in OpenSSL-LICENSE.txt.
License source: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.6.2/LICENSE.txt
Distributed as OpenSSL-Universal CocoaPod 3.6.2000 (exact dependency).
Packaging: https://github.com/krzyzanowskim/OpenSSL/tree/3.6.2000
Podspec: https://github.com/krzyzanowskim/OpenSSL/blob/3.6.2000/OpenSSL-Universal.podspec
Binary: https://github.com/krzyzanowskim/OpenSSL/releases/download/3.6.2000/OpenSSL.xcframework.zip
Binary SHA256: 37846a8bd302cb2443eff47f1045ab844d0cd40bf82cc6159cfad9aa5c3eff9e
The XCFramework contains ios-arm64 and ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator slices.
It is downloaded by CocoaPods, not committed here. ../PiSshOpenSSL.h selects the
framework namespace explicitly; no forwarding headers shadow that namespace.

These notices and licenses are included in the PiSshLicenses resource bundle.
